title: App shell — layout primitives starter
summary: Twelve foundational layout + atom primitives an agent typically needs when scaffolding a real app. Install once, then compose rather than hand-rolling `space-y-*` chains, `grid sm:grid-cols-*` breakpoints, dashed empty-state divs, or `rounded-full border` badge spans.
brief: Drop in the layout primitives an agent forgets — container width, vertical stack, responsive grid, breadcrumb back-links, timeline, empty state — so composition wins over hand-rolled utility chains.

steps.reason: Constrain page width — replaces hand-rolled `mx-auto max-w-*`
Horizontal wrap with gap — replaces `flex flex-wrap gap-*`
Explicit vertical gap when stack/cluster don't fit
Standard card surface — never roll `rounded-lg border bg-card` by hand
Status chip — replaces `rounded-full border text-xs` spans
Filter / topic chip variant of badge
Chronological list — replaces hand-rolled `<ol>` + absolute dots

checklist.check: Use `<Container size='md'>` for page-width constraints instead of `mx-auto max-w-*`.
Use `<Grid cols='auto-fit' minColWidth='280px'>` for responsive card grids — no more `sm:grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3` breakpoint chains.
Use `<Stack gap='…'>` for vertical rhythm instead of `space-y-*` utility chains.
Use `<Empty>` for empty states instead of dashed-border divs.
Use `<Breadcrumb>` for back-links instead of hand-rolled `←` anchors.
Use `<Timeline>` for chronological listings instead of `<ol>` + absolute-positioned dots.
[Container] Avoid: Wrapping a `Container` in another `Container` and getting an unexpectedly narrow column
[Container] Avoid: Using `padding="none"` and forgetting that children still need their own gutter — the parent contributes nothing
[Container] Avoid: Treating `lg` as the largest size — `xl` (66rem) and `full` are bigger
[Container] A11y: Container is presentational. Wrap in a semantic landmark (`<main>`, `<section>`, `<article>`) when the page structure needs it; Container itself renders a plain `<div>`.
[Stack] Avoid: Setting `gap="md"` then adding `mt-*` / `space-y-*` on individual children — pick one spacing system
[Stack] Avoid: Using `align="center"` and wondering why children expand to full width — that's the `stretch` default for cross-axis
[Stack] Avoid: Nesting Stack inside Stack with the same gap when one Stack with two children would suffice
[Stack] A11y: Stack is presentational. Wrap stacked navigation links in a `<nav>`, stacked form fields in a `<form>`, etc. — Stack does not contribute landmark semantics.
[Cluster] Avoid: Forgetting that `Cluster` wraps — adding `flex-nowrap` defeats the purpose; if you don't want wrap, use a flex row or `Stack` rotated
[Cluster] Avoid: Setting `align="baseline"` for icon+text rows where the icon's bbox doesn't have a baseline — use `center` instead
[Cluster] Avoid: Reaching for `Cluster` for tabular alignment — use `Grid` or a real `<table>` when columns must line up

[Cluster] A11y: Cluster is presentational. Lists of navigational items should be wrapped in `<nav>` (and ideally `<ul>` / `<li>`). Lists of tags can use a list element for screen-reader semantics; the visual wrap is independent.
[Grid] Avoid: Setting `cols={5}` and getting nothing — the preset only supports 1/2/3/4/6 (deliberate, to avoid odd visual rhythms); use `cols="auto-fit"` for arbitrary counts
[Grid] Avoid: Passing `cols="auto-fit"` without `minColWidth` — the default `16rem` may not match your design intent
[Grid] Avoid: Using `Grid` for two children when `Cluster` or `Stack` would communicate intent better
[Grid] A11y: Grid is presentational. If the grid renders a list of similar items, wrap in `<ul>`/`<li>` for screen-reader semantics — Grid only handles visual layout.
[Spacer] Avoid: Using `<Spacer />` between every child in a Stack — just set the Stack's `gap` instead
[Spacer] Avoid: Using `axis="both"` and getting a square block where you wanted a line — `both` is rare, usually you want vertical or horizontal
[Spacer] Avoid: Setting size="lg" on a horizontal spacer and getting nothing visible because the parent isn't a flex row — Spacer reserves space, it doesn't push siblings on its own
[Spacer] A11y: Spacer is `aria-hidden="true"` — screen readers skip it. Don't use a Spacer where a `Separator` would convey meaning (a thematic break should be `Separator`, not `Spacer`).
[Empty] Avoid: Using Empty without an action — leaves the user stuck
[Empty] Avoid: Long descriptions — keep to one sentence; this is a state surface, not documentation
[Empty] Avoid: Forgetting titleAs when the page already has an h2 above (heading hierarchy break)
[Empty] A11y: Wrapped in a region landmark labeled by the title (aria-labelledby + auto-generated id). Icon is decorative (aria-hidden). Pair the action with a Button that has a visible label.
[Card] Avoid: Nesting cards
[Card] Avoid: Using Card when a simple div with border would suffice
[Card] Avoid: Forgetting CardContent padding when placing forms inside
[Card] A11y: Card is a div by default. Add role='region' and aria-labelledby (pointing to CardTitle's id) for landmark cards. CardTitle renders h3 — ensure heading hierarchy is correct on the page.
[Separator] Avoid: Using as spacing instead of semantic separation
[Separator] Avoid: Forgetting orientation='vertical' needs parent height
[Separator] A11y: Set decorative=false if the separator conveys semantic meaning. Radix handles role='separator'.
[Badge] Avoid: Using destructive variant for non-error states
[Badge] Avoid: Badge text too long
[Badge] A11y: Purely decorative by default. Add role='status' for dynamic status badges.
[Tag] Avoid: Forgetting onRemove on a tag the user CAN dismiss — leaves the affordance invisible
[Tag] Avoid: Calling it Tag but rendering inside a list of static labels — confuses Tag (interactive) vs Badge (decorative) semantics
[Tag] Avoid: Wrapping the tag itself in a <button> — the dismiss button already handles its own click; double-button breaks accessibility

[Tag] A11y: Close button gets aria-label derived from children when they're a string ('Remove Urgent'). Override via removeLabel. Tag itself is a span — wrap in a list (`role='list'` + `role='listitem'`) when rendering N tags as a collection.
[Timeline] Avoid: Forgetting aria-label — the <ol> needs an accessible name to be understood as a feed
[Timeline] Avoid: Using duplicate event ids — breaks React keys and event reconciliation on re-render
[Timeline] Avoid: Stuffing the description with rich layouts that overflow the timeline rail — keep it short or move to a Card
[Timeline] Avoid: Setting status='error' on every event for emphasis — color loses meaning when overused
[Timeline] Avoid: Mixing controlled timestamps as Date objects without formatting — Timeline accepts ReactNode, so format upstream (date-fns) before passing in

[Timeline] A11y: Renders <ol> with the provided aria-label. The status-colored indicator and connector line are aria-hidden — meaning is carried entirely by the title/timestamp/description text. No aria-current; events are historical, not navigational. For >50 events consider a windowing solution outside Timeline.
[Breadcrumb] Avoid: Making the current page a link (use BreadcrumbPage)
[Breadcrumb] Avoid: Showing just one item (defeats the purpose)
[Breadcrumb] Avoid: Using plain text separators without aria-hidden

[Breadcrumb] A11y: Root <nav aria-label='breadcrumb'> creates a landmark. BreadcrumbPage has aria-current='page'. Separators are aria-hidden (decorative). BreadcrumbEllipsis is decorative (SVG aria-hidden) with a sr-only 'More pages' label.
